pattern_name: Passive (all tenses) + causative have/get something done
pattern_name_ar: المبني للمجهول (كل الأزمنة) + الصيغة السببية have/get something done
formula: be (any tense) + participle · is being / has been / had been / will be / to be / modal + be · have/get + object + participle
formula_visual: [The road is being repaired] // [I had my hair cut]
when_to_use: The passive works in every tense by changing 'be': is repaired, is being repaired, has been repaired, had been repaired, will be repaired, must be repaired, to be repaired. The causative 'have/get + object + participle' means you arranged for someone ELSE to do it: 'I had my hair cut.'
when_to_use_ar: المجهول يعمل في كل الأزمنة بتغيير 'be'. والصيغة السببية 'have/get + مفعول + التصريف الثالث' تعني أنك رتّبت لشخص آخر أن يفعلها: 'I had my hair cut.'
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic forms the passive by internal vowel change with no auxiliary, so learners drop 'be' or 'been'. The causative is harder still: 'I cut my hair' and 'I had my hair cut' both translate similarly, but in English the first means you did it yourself.

examples.en: The road is being repaired at the moment.
The house has already been sold.
The building had been abandoned for years.
I had my hair cut yesterday.
I need to get my car fixed.

common_errors.explanation: The passive always needs a form of 'be' before the participle.

common_errors.wrong: I cut my hair yesterday. (at the barber's)
common_errors.correct: I had my hair cut yesterday.
common_errors.explanation: If someone else did it for you, use the causative.
Word order: have + OBJECT + participle. 'I had cut' is the past perfect, a different meaning.

quick_rule: Passive = be (in any tense) + participle. Causative = have/get + OBJECT + participle (someone else did it for you).
quick_rule_ar: المجهول = be (بأي زمن) + التصريف الثالث. السببية = have/get + المفعول + التصريف الثالث (شخص آخر فعلها لك).
mnemonic: No 'be', no passive. Object BEFORE the participle in causatives.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 9 you drilled flat auxiliary chains and causative stress. Say 'I had my hair CUT' with the stress on the final participle — that stress is what marks it as a service.
